# Lockheed pushes PAC-3 MSE output toward 750 a year as RTX scales Patriot radars

Aviation Week, June 9, 2026

Lockheed Martin is expanding its Camden, Arkansas and Grand Prairie, Texas facilities to raise PAC-3 MSE interceptor production from roughly 550 interceptors in 2025 toward 650 in 2027 and 750 per year by 2028, executives said. The interceptor is fired from the Patriot system, whose radars and launchers are built by RTX's Raytheon unit, so the two companies' capacity plans are linked.

RTX, for its part, has said it is doubling output of the GEM-T interceptor for Patriot and ramping the new LTAMDS radar. Analysts at the conference noted that Lockheed's PAC-3 backlog gives it multi-year visibility that RTX's radar business lacks, while RTX benefits from the larger installed base of Patriot fire units.

THAAD interceptor production is also rising, with the company guiding to 96 interceptors in 2026 under a multiyear Missile Defense Agency award.
